messages.text: You answering tonight or is the blue-star circus already making you holler
I can talk at 7:15 if the fourth quarter has not ruined my manners.
Good. I need somebody else mad about that offensive line.
Save one complaint for me. I still have church clothes to hang up and supper to warm.
Did you see Father Miguel changed the fish fry setup time? I put it on the parish page this afternoon!
I saw it after Gina tagged me. I only opened FB long enough to mark the food table and check Aunt Rose's photos.
Good. Also look at the little painted herb markers I sent you from that garden account. They would be cute near your basil.
Saved those and one porch-pot idea. Then I closed it before the reels swallowed my evening.
You already beat the crowd didnt you
Yesterday morning. In and out before the coffee cooled.
Bet you still split the sheet and made it complicated
I kept the ones who can count a budget and crossed off the loud school-board fellow. Roads and police staffing mattered more than his slogans.
You still got that porch light on a timer or did the bulb finally quit
Timer is fine. I swapped the bulb Sunday and checked the back latch while I was out there.
Good. Those pickups cutting through your road after work are moving like they are late for kickoff.
That bend by the mailbox is worse every week. I wait for a long clear gap before backing out now.
I left that slim paperback on your porch. The one with the city under glass and the strange insurance bureau in chapter two.
Perfect timing. I was about to make tea and read a few pages before lights out.
The bureau scene made me think of how you explain coverage without frightening people.
That is going in my little notebook. I need a better opening example for the risk chapter.
found that old brochure from the big office east of here while cleaning a drawer
The one you told me to sleep on before I signed anything?
same one. you kept your own name on the door and still outlasted half the people in that room
Bring it to lunch if it is not too dusty. Eighteen Marches at the agency deserves a laugh.
That shop owner called me too. She said the carrier offered the cheaper package.
It leaves a hole in the roof claim. I would rather lose the sale than hand her that.
Figured you would say that. Lunch Friday and bring the notes if you want another set of eyes
Thank you. I am also reworking the proposal page so it shows the gaps plainly, not just the price.
Lunch Thursday still good
Yes. I may be ten minutes late if the bakery owner's renewal call runs long. I have to compare the building limit, GL, and the delivery van changes before I leave.
Bring the notes. Two carrier sites will tell you two different stories as usual
Already logged both quotes in Epic and emailed her the cleaner version. I'll call her after the underwriter answers.
Elise from the little boutique called again. Found one more policy folder in her mother's desk.
I will handle it after dinner. I already put the bench lamp on low and left the blue canvas out.
Good. Do the paperwork tomorrow if tonight gets heavy.
Just a few quiet keys first, then that narrow orange streak. It steadies the room.
Can you look at the county storm form before I send it to Mrs. Alvarez? It asks for receipts, photos, and the shutoff notice.
Yes. Tell her to include only the freezer loss and hotel night, not the whole grocery bill. They are checking dates against the outage map.
That sounds fair. I will help her scan everything after lunch.
Good. I like that they ask for proof and still move fast for people who got hit hardest.
I found another envelope from Mom's blue folder. It has the old appointment cards clipped to a stack of benefit forms.
Keep it for me. I want to compare it with the notes I made when I was driving her back and forth.
There is also a receipt from that quiet office you went to alone after the service. Do you want that shredded or saved?
Save it in the back pocket for now. I only went a few times, but I still like having the dates straight.
The parish form asks if volunteers have had fingerprint cards before. I only remember that traffic ticket you had outside Aledo years ago!
That and the fender-bender report on 199 are about the whole list for me. The deputy was polite both times.
Good. Aunt Rosa used to bring up Tommy's old courthouse mess like it happened to all of us, but he was barely around.
Exactly. I saw him at weddings, not Sunday dinner. I wouldn't even know what year that was without Gina's binder.
For the parish table, are you putting Deluca-Benedetti by the biscotti tray again?
Yes. I found Grandma Rosa's card with Calabria written in her old hand, so I will tuck a copy under the tray.
I found that little recipe card with Nonna's red pot stains on it. It says basil last, not oregano first!
If I bring those two lavender starts Saturday, do you still have room along the sunny side by the kitchen window?
That explains why mine never smells right by noon. I can hear her saying mangia before I even open the drawer.
Yes, that strip gets sun most of the day. I moved the clay pots off the porch so the little bed is clear.
Good! Use the almond ones, not the anise batch. People asked for those last year.
Good! I will wrap them in newspaper after my bakery shift. Your place always smells better after March.
The card also has Nonno's old town scribbled on the back, the one near Reggio. I will bring it to coffee.
Bring them when you come for coffee. I will leave the side gate unlatched if I am still rinsing trays.
Bring it. I can read the food words and the family sayings, but that handwriting beats me.
Do you still have that roll of silver paper tucked in the back room? I only need a strip for the festival basket.
Yes, it is behind the canvases. I can cut you some after I finish this corner section on the folding table.
No rush! If the little pieces are spread out, leave them. I can get the paper from you at coffee.
The print on this trail notice is tiny. I can send a photo before Saturday if that helps.
Please do. My extra pair is in the kitchen drawer, so I would rather read it at home.
I will take a clear picture. No need to bring anything special for the walk.
The scissor-tailed pair was back by the fence line this evening.
I almost turned around there just to watch the light settle over the pasture.
Saturday should be clear. I can bring the binoculars if you want to start on the west trail.
Yes, west trail first. The open stretch near the old windmill is worth the early start.
quiet table friday? bring that list of potters hair folks and little shop owners
Yes. I also want your eye on the one-page outline for Maya and Tessa. They keep asking how to handle first renewal calls without sounding canned.
good. dont make it fancy. give them scripts then let them listen to you work one
That is the plan. After lunch I am blocking two hours for the guide draft before the day disappears.
still at your desk?
Last renewal file. Then I am putting the laptop away and finding the pretzel twists.
good. eat something with more backbone than twists
I paused the chef judges at the sauce round. That and the orange bag are waiting for me.
Fresh basil won this morning. Nonna would fuss at both of us if we used the jar today!
Then fresh it is. I will bring a container when we do coffee in Mineral Wells.
Good. Gina asked if you and Marco can keep March 21 open, and Sofia texted that she can come after her Saturday shift.
I will ask Marco Sunday. Tell Sofia I am glad she can make it.
If I bring the sirloins Sunday, you doing that tomato thing on the side again?
Maybe. I already have onions, peppers, and half a can of tomatoes open, so it may turn into Monday pasta too.
Good. Waste not. I will bring enough for Gina if she shows.
Bring the smaller pack. I am stretching this week with beans and soup in the freezer.
Can we do coffee after the parish table setup Friday? I can meet halfway if your office day is packed!
Friday works if I slide my first client call to 10:30. I still have a few PTO hours and sick hours showing in the portal, so I am trying not to burn any of them for errands.
Good, save them. I will bring the biscotti recipe and you can tell me if the basil plant survived.
Deal. The March 15 deposit should land before then, so lunch is on me if the delayed shop add-on finally shows.
You still at that desk or did they finally let you go home
Just shut the file drawer. Timesheet says 46.25, and I still have Saturday notes to clean up before Mass.
Same place since Romo had a baby face and they still make you fight your own schedule battles
Pretty much. Handbook, Renee, and my own calendar. No magic referee.
Saturday still looks clear if we start from the north lot at 7:30.
That works. I will bring almonds and the small thermos again.
Good. I cleaned the Nikon pair, so we can pause by the creek if those little gray ones are back.
Only if you promise not to quiz me on calls before coffee.
Lunch is still Tuesday if my knee behaves. Bring that yellow pad if you want me to look at your March numbers.
I will. I have the CU drafts listed and the Visa payoff set for the 14th, before the statement date.
Good. Keep the card clean and let the little market account do its quiet work.
That is the plan. The cash cushion is staying untouched unless something truly breaks.
The office phones are wild again. People are forwarding screenshots from Facebook and asking us if they should cancel appointments.
I would rather read Dr. Nguyen's portal note than somebody's cousin's post. Send me the Baylor page you said your office keeps at the desk.
Sent. It is the plain one-page explainer, no drama. Also remember to ask them to update your card when you go.
Already put it with my insurance cards. I muted that thread from Aunt Rosa before breakfast.
If the roads glaze over Sunday night, would it bother you if I used the key and took the back room?
Use it. I washed the sheets after Christmas, and nobody has touched that room since.
Thank you. I will bring groceries and not rearrange your quiet little system.
Groceries are fine. Just text before you pull in so I can move the bill folders off the kitchen table.
Do you still have Nonna's lemon knot recipe? The St. Clare table is short on sweets for next Saturday.
I have it in the blue binder. I can bake two trays Friday night and drop them before the 5:00.
Perfect! I will put you by the pasta and bread side again unless Teresa moves us.
That corner works. I will bring a roll of quarters for the donation jar too.
The trail should be dry by 7:30. I can bring the small binoculars if you still want a quiet loop before the phones start.
Yes, please. I made a two-column list at 5:15 and it helped, but I still need to move my feet before touching the renewal stack.
Then we will keep the pace steady and stop at the feeder near the creek. Coffee afterward only if you have room in the morning.
Radar looks clear until almost 10. Same 7:30 route by the creek?
Coffee after. I put Gina's lab-result call on the list too, so I will be better company once I have some air.
Yes. I did the little floor routine first, so I should loosen up by the second bend.
Good. I will bring the binoculars. If the wind turns, we can shorten it and still get coffee.
That works. I already got out Tuesday and Thursday, so no heroics today.
The wind is already up, so I am moving slowly this morning. Are you still coming for the 7:30 loop?
Trail is still muddy. I can do coffee first if you want to finish the ProPublica piece you printed.
Yes. I was up late with the old Yamaha after that awful stack of forms, but I slept fine once I was done.
That works. I am halfway through it with toast, and I marked the part about stop reports for you.
Good. Bring your gloves. I will bring the binoculars and we can keep the first mile quiet.
Bring the pages. I also saved that interview with the former chief; it is better heard than skimmed.
Quiet sounds perfect. I left Night Train by the stereo so I may put it back on when I get home.
I will. No comment threads for me before breakfast.
Lunch still 12:45? bring that shop account folder if you want another set of eyes
Yes. I put the dates into the account screen this morning, but I am bringing the legal-pad version too.
Good. Paper catches what screens hide.
I also drew the three paint coats for the owner. It keeps the blank spots from sounding scarier than they are.
Defense forgot how tackling works. Call at 7:15 unless this gets uglier.
7:15 works. I need your vote on Gina's Fort Worth lunch plan.
If Tony is driving from Denton, pick somewhere with parking. Elena complained last time.
Noted. I will tell Gina after we talk.
The light on the trail this morning reminded me of that blue shop window in Fredericksburg you showed me.
The article I sent has a quiet map of temple moss areas around Kyoto. It says the November mornings are thinner before tour buses start.
I still have those photos on my phone. That little loop was easier than I expected for two days away.
I saved it. I am only letting myself compare dates after I do the little Sunday transfer.
That sounds sensible. Santa Fe can wait its turn if the airfare page behaves.
Are you still keeping the New Mexico gallery list, or did the house and policy bills win for now?
Keeping the list. I just moved it out of the current month until the numbers stop arguing with me.
lunch still Tuesday? quieter place if you need to bring papers
Tuesday works. I may bring my little sheet because February closed at 4,300 after the dentist and the car.
one ugly month does not mean change the whole plan
Exactly. I am leaving the automatic transfer alone until I see March cleanly in the bank app.
Did you get the two little bottles after work, or should I swing by Walgreens when I go for Mama's birthday candles?
I got them Wednesday. One goes by the coffee maker and one stays with the evening pillbox.
Good. Also check that March paystub line before the new card starts pulling again. Those little charges sneak up.
Already looked. The office plan took its usual chunk, and the card covered the counter total.
The county meeting packet is up. The EMS contract and deputy vacancies are both on page 6.
Thank you. I printed those pages with the clinic-cost chart and the school roof item.
You may want to read the last speaker list carefully. Some of it sounds more like theater than problem solving.
That is exactly what wears me out. I want numbers, road crews, class sizes, and response times.
I found the strawberry cake order. They can write just "62" on top if you do not want all those candles.
Please do that. I do not need the smoke alarm going off at my own table.
Marco asked whether we are doing it at your house or at Lucia's halfway place. I told him Springtown is easier for most of us.
My house is fine. I will put Mama's pink platter out if you bring the old photo envelope from the Weatherford box.
Storm line looks ugly tonight. You got that loose brick by the front step fixed yet?
Not until Friday. I put the heavy pot in front of it and brought the smaller succulents under the porch.
No upstairs roof to worry over at least. Text me if the power blinks.
Will do. I already checked the back latch and charged the lantern.
Marco found that photo of us outside Springtown High. You had the same work bag even then, I swear.
That bag came later, but the habit of driving the same roads did not.
You still know every shortcut from Weatherford to my place. I am adding your agency party card to the birthday stack.
Thank you. Keep the card simple. No speech about me staying put, please.
Aunt Rosa's papers have three different dollar columns. I do not want to tell her the wrong one.
Send me photos of the front page and the page with the limits. I will write the order on a pad first, then I will check it against the saved record.
Sent. Thank you. She keeps asking which part pays first.
I will mark it like primer, color, and clear coat so she can see what sits on top of what.
I opened the packet and your yellow notes saved me. Can you tell me again why you crossed out the first plan?
The low premium looked good until the specialist visits showed up. I circled the part they hide on page six.
Of course you read page six. Also Marco wants to sit by the window at the birthday lunch, not by the TV.
I already drew him between you and Lucia. Less game commentary, more cake.
Good morning! I put aside the parish handout from last night. Deacon Tom added notes from the listening table.
Thank you. I can read it with my coffee before I leave, then call you after supper.
Perfect. The part from the mother on the east side stayed with me.
My dryer made a terrible sound and the repair man says $389. I nearly dropped the phone.
That is exactly the kind of ugly surprise I keep that side account for. I would rather grumble and pay it than carry it around.
You are steadier than me! I put the festival cannoli money in the wrong envelope again.
My envelopes are plain: house, Toyota, card paid clean, then the six-month column. Boring, but it keeps me sleeping.
I found Nonna's lemon cookie card in the church folder. Sending you a picture tomorrow!
Please do. I just put the metronome away and have We Get Requests on low, so I am finally ready to look at something sweet.
At this hour? Your house must be peaceful tonight.
It is. No one here to mind a few careful runs before bed.
You still reading those government charts before Walgreens? Just go or don't go.
I am checking Dr. Nguyen's message first. The chart tells me which box to ask for, not Facebook.
Fair. But if that group chat starts yelling again I am blaming you for leaving me in there.
I left it yesterday. All caps before coffee is not a civic duty.
You going to that council thing again? You and your homework packets.
Only because page 6 finally says who sees the camera files and how long they keep them. That matters.
As long as they don't turn every mistake into a circus.
A clear file, a fair review, and real follow-through when someone lies on paperwork. That protects everyone better than rumors.
Scanned that card. Stamp says 1926 clear as day. Other corner looks like Napoli, not sure.
That fits the story Dad always told over the simmering pot, before he made us grate cheese.
You still remember what Nonna yelled when we stole bread?
Something like basta and then my name. After that I just remember the spoon waving.
For Saturday, do you want me to park at your place or by the trailhead?
Trailhead may be easier. At my driveway, people are coming over that hill too fast before coffee time.
Trailhead it is. I will bring the binoculars and we can leave your porch lamp on until we get back.
That works. I will lock up and meet you at 7:30.
saw your note on LinkedIn about the boutique renewal checklist. plain and useful
Thanks. I put work things there and leave the family/parish updates on FB where they belong.
wise. keep the client crowd from seeing everybody's casserole schedule
Exactly. I checked LinkedIn, answered two comments, and got out before lunch.
You sounded wound tight after that boutique account call. Eat something before you open the next file
I closed the laptop. Ten names left for tomorrow, written in order. I am putting paint on that little blue canvas instead of circling the same numbers.
Good. The files will still be ugly in the morning. Blue canvas is better tonight
I found the Taos inn card in my drawer! If you still want September, I can call my friend about the little casita.
Hold it for me, please. I am trying to build the fall calendar around fewer regular appointments and more work I can do with a laptop.
Good. Bring your notebook when we get coffee. I want to see the pages about painters and food trucks.
Deal. I also owe Maya and Tessa the checklist before then, so coffee may include red pen time.
Gina says you are digging through old family dates. Don't let Tommy make himself sound important from 17 years back.
I'm just checking the year. He made one bad drive after that lake party and the rest of us only heard about it at reunions.
Right. In our house it was speeding slips, Dad grumbling, and paying the county clerk. Nothing dramatic.
That matches what I remember. Even my little stop near Weatherford was just license, warning, and go home.
Found Dad's old folder. Ship copy says Napoli to New York, 1921. You want a photo?
Send it. I am matching those papers with Mom's side before I finish that clinic portal history page.
Mom's notes were all Ireland and Pennsylvania coal country. That sound right?
That is what Gina and I found too. I will keep the copies together.
Still good for the trail at 7:30 tomorrow? I can bring the extra binoculars.
Yes. I told Daniel dinner is another night. I like him, but I need Saturday morning kept clear.
That sounds fair. Clear words early usually spare everyone trouble later.
Exactly. Coffee after, then I need to finish the water bill and insurance folder before lunch.
Tuesday lunch still on? I want somewhere quiet enough to hear you without shouting
Yes. Yesterday Cafe at 12:15? I have a morning loop with Maribel first, so I will not book anything tight.
Fine by me. Bring the small-account question too if it is still bothering you
Bring that outline to lunch if you still want blunt notes
I will. The first section is about getting clients to picture risk before they see a premium number.
Good. Stories sell if they stay plain
Lunch moved to 12:40. knee clinic ran long
Exactly. Last night's book gave me a cleaner way to talk about a shop owner planning for the one impossible Tuesday.
That helps. I am at 31 hours before Friday afternoon, so I can finish two small-business renewals first.
You were doing those accounts before half the new producers could spell binder
Renee found the old March 2008 folder for the pin order. I told her to use the plain silver one.
If the ice comes in tonight, I may bring a bag. Is the spare bed reachable?
Reachable, yes. I need to stack the framed pieces against the closet and slide the little card table closer to the window.
I can sleep around your projects. Just save the border pieces from my elbow.
I already put a cookie sheet over that side. You will have a path.
Are you still coming for coffee after the parish table meeting? I saved you two lemon knots!
I am, but I need to finish one contractor certificate and a new-driver change first. The portal froze right when I got to the VIN screen.
Of course it did. I will ask Father Ben to hold the food boxes until you get here.
Thank you. If the help desk picks up, I can email both files and leave by 10:30.
I found the peach jam from Stonewall in the pantry! Was that from your little overnight with the wildflowers?
Yes, from that stop after Johnson City. I should have bought two jars.
Bring it when we do coffee. And don't toss those Santa Fe chapel notes, please. We can still talk tiles and saints over cannoli.
The notes are safe. They're just sitting behind the tax packet and the roofing estimate right now.
You coming by Weatherford or did the hawks steal you again
Not stolen. I stopped south of Springtown where the road opens up. Two of them were circling over the cut field.
Figures. Supper is at 6:30 if you quit staring at fences and clouds.
I will make it. The clouds are doing that copper edge thing, so give me ten minutes.
You watching that kitchen contest again or still buried in forms?
Both. Muted until I finish these two endorsements.
That is not dinner
I know. Pretzels first, brisket tacos if El Jefe is still open.
The coffee place was crowded after the trail. Did you get your beans somewhere else?
I went home and ground the darker roast Lucia talked me into. Better than standing in that line.
That sounds nicer anyway. Are you still cooking this afternoon?
Yes, roasting a chicken and saving the bones. I want broth ready for soup by Monday.
You were quiet after coffee. Did the closed shop window on Main bring back that October week?
A little. I came home and played the soft left-hand part twice.
That sounds like a better choice than opening the file boxes right away.
The canvas is almost all night blue now. The orange is just a thread across it.
Do you still want me to save the ceramic festival flyer from Santa Fe? It came in the mail pile at Mom's old box.
Yes, please. I put another $25 aside this morning, so the folder gets to stay on the kitchen desk.
I will bring it Tuesday. Also, the Kyoto clipping with the maple walk is still in your cookbook, unless you moved it.
Leave it there. I like seeing it when I am being sensible with the checkbook.
I saved you two zeppole from the parish table! Are you heading straight home after coffee?
Yes, I want the TV on by 1:05. Marco will fuss if I miss his halftime call.
Then take the pastries and run. Orange hat or blue shirt today?
Orange until dinner, blue if Marco starts texting complaints.
I can bring coffee Friday and help with the old forms if you want. Those little clinic stickers always peel off the folders!
That would help. Some of the pages still have my notes about which desk needed which signature.
And if the Dr. Ramos cards make you feel funny, we can put them aside. No need to read everything in one sitting.
Thank you. Those were only a handful of Thursdays, but I remember being worn thin then.
Menu at Cattleman's is still printed for ants.
Then sit me near the window. I left the little fold-up pair in the car last time.
Fine. Window table. Wear whatever, nobody there cares.
That is the easiest part of the evening.
That mechanic in Weatherford still treating you right or did he win the lottery off your Buick
He was fair. The car line just made last month's bank total look ridiculous next to my 3,700 to 3,900 rows.
Rows. Of course you got rows for it.
Laugh all you want. The rows keep me from touching money I set aside for boring surprises.
I confirmed the table for Saturday at 12:30. Marco said he can come if the weather stays decent.
Good. I will bring the lemon cookies and Lucia's basil clipping if it survives my kitchen window.
Elena and Sofia are riding together. Tony said he will meet us there because he has errands first.
That should work. Text me if the head count changes before Friday.
I still have your spare key on my ring. Do you want me to stop by Friday and water the porch trays before I go to Fort Worth?
That would help. The lavender by the back walk is fine, but the shallow succulent tray dries out fast.
I can do that. I will also bring in anything left on the front mat so it is not sitting there all afternoon.
Thank you. The payment packet from the bank may come this week, so just set it on the studio desk if you see it.
Found Daddy's old utility badge in the garage. Same box had Mama's school ribbon from Aledo.
Save both for me. Gina is making a folder with all the courthouse copies and old Parker County things.
You still want me to look for the Springtown school pictures too?
Yes. Everything before my first agency job seems to fit in three places: Weatherford, Springtown, and Fort Worth.
Trail should be dry by Saturday. I can bring the field guide if you still want to compare the calls.
Please do. I have been trying to draw the sound patterns beside the names so they stick.
That sounds like one of your notebooks. Coffee afterward?
Yes, but I need to leave by 10:15. I promised Lucia I would test the sauce card before she prints it.
The art museum posted the watercolor workshop preview. It reminded me of the seed catalog page you liked.
I saw it on IG with that patio rose sketch. I saved both and one jazz trio clip for later.
That sounds like a pleasant five minutes before the walk. I will bring the binoculars.
Five minutes is about my limit there. I still need to check the Springtown notice on FB before I leave.
Rosa at the frame shop asked about that March loan list you mentioned
Send her the chamber link, but tell her not to skip the sales drop sheet. They are asking for Feb bank statements and a 30-day plan.
Good. No blank checks then
Exactly. If the shop can show the hit and show how the money keeps payroll going, I am glad the town set money aside.
The patient portal kicked back Aunt Lena's family history page because one section was left blank.
If it is the same page I did, I left that section empty and used the line that matched Dad and Mom's papers.
That helps. I will bring the old folder when I come by after work.
The nurse said they may not call about Uncle Pete until Monday. I know waiting all weekend is hard. Did Dr. Moore ever call you back after your checkup?
She left a portal note: labs fine, keep the walking, sleep, and meals boring for a bit. Nothing added.
That is good. Please do not spend all night refreshing Pete's chart. Say your rosary and text me after the first decade if you are still awake.
I will. I already wrote down what we actually know and what can wait until Monday. Calling you helped.
Use the last of the fresh basil before it wilts! It will make even plain noodles taste like Sunday.
That is the plan. I have the sauce warming with the parmesan heel, and the rest goes over tomorrow's lunch.
Good girl. Did the beans come out soft this time?
Yes, finally. Half for tonight, half tucked away with the broth.
You done working or still chained to that phone
Almost done. Last call was a family adding a teen driver, and now I am fixing a restaurant payroll estimate before the carrier locks the quote.
Sounds like a Friday headache. Game starts at 7
I know. I put both notes in the CRM and sent the restaurant owner the signature link, so I should be off the phone soon.
your old small-shop account called me by mistake again. still asks for you first
I will call her after renewals. That was one of the two accounts you handed me when I stayed here.
best handoff I made. fancy building would have made you wear shoes that hurt
And I would have missed the people who still call the Weatherford number before lunch.
Heard Parker County may get ugly weather Sunday night. You still doing that claims sheet table if roofs take a hit
If Teresa opens the hall, yes. I kept the plain-language handouts from last year and can bring my stapler.
Good. Folks listen better when it is someone they already know from the supper line.
That is why I like doing it there. They ask real questions once the coffee is poured.
Before I forget, are you still free for the family birthday lunch on March 29? I know you blocked several Saturdays lately.
I am free that day. Today is the 50-plus roundtable notes, then the draft packet for the two younger ones.
You always end up helping people find their footing. Bring the dessert list too, please.
I will. I am also sketching the part about tiny studios and weekend vendors, so I may come with sticky notes on my sleeves.
For tomorrow, do you want me to bring the basil or just the salad? Marco said you are doing the early pot.
Bring basil if you have good leaves. I will start garlic before church so the house has time to smell right.
I also found the parish heritage form. It asks for the old village and year arrived. I wrote 1920-something and left the spelling blank.
Good call. I can say it the way Aunt Rose did, but I would not bet on spelling it.
Do you still want me to call after 9, or is that your quiet time with the lamp and book?
After 9:30 is better. I want to finish the chapter where the map keeps changing.
That sounds like one of your client examples waiting to happen.
Already scribbled a note: people plan better when the map is honest about moving.
I left the casserole in your fridge. The envelope from the boutique family is on the counter, unopened.
Thank you. I saw it and went straight to the piano before I touched it.
Call me before you read it if you need to. I mean it.
I will. I may put another wash of blue down first, but the orange line stays thin.
I put your sauce container by the side door like you said. Did not want to leave it on the porch too long!
Thank you. I had the front light on and the side door bolted, so I saw it right away.
Also, mercy, the cars on your block were zipping past. I held the rail before stepping down.
Yes, I tell visitors to use the side path and take their time now.
Lunch Monday or you hiding from me until the Cowboys draft talk starts
Monday is fine. I moved my desk day home in the morning so I can take the BlueCross call before driving toward Weatherford.
Bring that folder then. Gina said you understand those forms better than the rest of us.
I will. Just remind me not to count on that small-business add-on until the 31st run; last month it changed the total by over 1,000.
Trail should be dry by 7:30. Do you need to stop anywhere on the way to coffee?
Just CVS for a new pill splitter. The tiny morning tablet keeps crumbling when I cut it.
Light wind this morning. The pond trail may be better than the gravel loop.
